title: Solid state pelletizing for Bi-doped strontium molybdate synthesis and photocatalytic application
author: Acosta-Vergara, Torres-Palma, et al.

steps.title: Prepare Rhodamine B solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve Rhodamine B in deionized water to obtain a 10 mg L⁻¹ solution and make up the volume to 200 mL in a double‑layer glass tumbler.

steps.title: Add photocatalyst and adjust pH
steps.instruction: Add 0.2 g of the Sr₁₋₃ₓBi₂ₓΦₓMoO₄ photocatalyst (x = 0.15 for the optimal test) to the RhB solution and adjust the suspension pH to 3.0 using dilute acid or base as needed.

steps.title: Establish adsorption equilibrium
steps.instruction: Place the tumbler on a magnetic stirrer set to approximately 400 rpm and stir the suspension for about 30 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Set up irradiation system
steps.instruction: Position a 350 W Philips HPL‑N lamp (emits at 365 nm, photon energy ≈ 4 eV) above the tumbler, connect a water‑recirculation cooling system to maintain the reaction temperature at 40.0 ± 1 °C, and start the corundum air‑diffuser aeration system to supply excess oxygen.

steps.title: Irradiate and collect time‑point samples
steps.instruction: Turn on the UV lamp and irradiate the suspension for a total of 30 min, withdrawing aliquots at 1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 20 and 30 min.

steps.title: Filter withdrawn samples
steps.instruction: Immediately filter each collected aliquot through a suitable membrane filter to remove the catalyst particles, then seal the filtrate in clean test tubes.

steps.title: Measure absorbance
steps.instruction: Record the UV‑Vis absorbance of each filtered sample at 554 nm using a Unico 2800 spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Calculate decolorization percentage
steps.instruction: Using the initial absorbance (A₀) and the absorbance at each time point (Aₜ), compute the decolorization D = [(A₀ − Aₜ)/A₀] × 100 % for each sample.

steps.title: Perform catalyst reuse cycles (optional)
steps.instruction: After the first run with x = 0.15, recover the catalyst by filtration, dry it, and repeat the degradation assay under the same conditions for a second and third cycle to evaluate possible adsorption effects.

description:
The photocatalytic activity of the Sr1−3xBi2xΦxMoO4 system was investigated for oxidation of Rhodamine B. showed for all compositions a pseudo-first-order kinetic model, with the concentration of RhB changing according to the rate law, Eq. (2).(2)C=C0e−ktwhere C is the concentration of RhB at time t, C0 is the initial concentration of RhB and k is the reaction rate. The sample with x=0.15 presented a best adjust when oxidizing RhB in an aqueous medium at pH 3.0. In the Fig. 8a is showed that for a stoichiometric X = 0.15 and 0.20, the degradation is higher with relationship to Photolysis. However, for stoichiometric X = 0.05, 0.10 and 0.25 the degradation does not enhance. This behavior is correlated with minor value Eg and minor particle size. In studies on photocatalysis processes, comparison of the results of the photolysis, adsorption and photocatalytic mechanisms is important. Thus, the mentioned processes were respectively differentiated in the experiments in the presence of UV radiation, but without a catalyst to assay the photolysis process and in dark condition to evaluate the adsorption process. Based on the 4.1%, 20.4%, and 92.7% removal efficiency for adsorption, photolysis, and photocatalysis, respectively, RhB removal by Sr1−3xBi2x∅xMoO4
X = 0.15 occurs mainly through photocatalytic degradation. The effects of initial Sr1−3xBi2x∅xMoO4 (x = 0.05- 0.25), pH (3, 5, 7, 9), dosses catalyst (20, 50, 100, 200, 300 mg), and UV-C irradiation time (0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30 min) were optimized in a batch photoreactor, using RhB with 10 mg/L, figure b, c, d and e. The photoreactor was a rectangular cubic shape, made from Plexiglas, and had internal dimensions of 50 cm (length), 25 cm (width), and 2.5 cm (height), an applicable volume of 300 mL, and three UV lamps (low pressure, 6 W, Philips) that were placed on top of the reactor.
